properties.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco / Mission Rock Partners, adopted April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m. D1/D2 split from Figure 1.1 (p.10) and the Block D standards sheet (Appendix p.190).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Mission Rock Design Controls' own Figure 6.2 (Maximum Height Plan, p.151) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar and street grid, not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 5 real street-intersection control points (3rd St x Channel St, 3rd St x Long Bridge St, 3rd St x Mission Rock St, Bridgeview Way x Mission Rock St, Terry A. Francois Blvd x Mission Rock St), fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py and matched to their pixel positions in the diagram, then fit as a least-squares affine transform (never fewer than 5 points spanning the whole site, not just 1-2 nearby anchors). Cross-validated against the diagram's own printed scale bar and against the real, independently-confirmed positions of Verde, The Canyon, Building B, and Visa HQ (Building G) -- all four fell inside their correct named blocks under this transform, which is what caught and fixed an earlier, much worse-fitting 4-point version of this same transform (a block letter read one row off, producing 75m of error) before it was used for anything. Residual error against the 5 control points is roughly 3-13m. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (found via join_approximate.py's new MAJOR CLIP warning, added after a Pier 70 investigation prompted by the user): confirmed via direct satellite comparison that this block's SW corner sits squarely on a real, clearly-marked street crosswalk/intersection (3rd St x Mission Rock St) -- 44% of the raw trace was inside the buffered real-street layer. Clipped via shapely difference() against the real-street buffer and simplified the resulting curved corner to a clean 5-vertex shape; area dropped from ~2,640 to ~1,423 sq m. This removes roughly half the block, which is a large change -- flagged as needing a second look at the block's other 3 corners against the diagram (not done here) if area under-recovery turns out to matter for tower massing. RETRACED 2026-09-17 (brief docs/briefs/mission-rock-geometry.md; definition of done in docs/site-definition-of-done.md). (1) SOURCE. This file's source_doc_urls pointed at the March 2012 'Design + Development Revised Proposal' (90 pages, no Figure 6.2) while the text cited the Design Controls, so the original pixel measurements could not be reproduced. Redone from the adopted Mission Rock Design Controls (April 24, 2018, sfport.com), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151), rendered ONCE at 300 dpi to data/manual/_reference/mission_rock_dc_p151.png (3300x2550 px, full page). Every pixel measurement below is from that one render. (2) TRANSFORM (one for the whole figure). Since this file was first traced, the Assessor subdivided Seawall Lot 337 (recorded 2020-06-12, mapped 2021-04-13): the four Phase 1 blocks are real lots -- A/The Canyon 8719B002, G/Visa 8719A008, B 8719C003, F/Verde 8719C001 -- whose recorded areas match the plan's block areas within 3%. The figure's drawn corners of A, B, F and G (colour contours, OpenCV) were matched to those 16 real lot corners and a least-squares affine transform fitted: RMS residual 0.67 m, worst corner 1.39 m (n=16); scale 0.2570 m/px (x) and 0.2598 m/px (y), ratio 0.989; axis angle 89.88 deg, i.e. no shear. The figure's own printed 200 ft scale bar measures 239 px on the same render = 0.255 m/px, agreeing within 2%. lon = 2.9127666757282e-06*px + 2.2156884853242e-07*py + (-122.39479060102); lat = 1.6823215817497e-07*px + -2.3273617315092e-06*py + 37.77752553008. (3) VALIDATION on real lines NOT used in the fit: traced C and D west corners fall 0.2-2.4 m from the 3rd Street property line (west edge of the undivided remainder lot 8719A006); D and H south corners 0.1-1.5 m from the Mission Rock Street property line (south edge of 8719A006); J, I and H east corners 1.1-2.8 m from the Terry A Francois Boulevard property line (east edge of 8719A006 / west edge of the TAFB lot 8719A003); the traced Block K corners fall 0.7-1.3 m from the corners of the lobe of the park lot 8719A005 that K occupies. Bearing check, the shear test that Pier 70's point check missed: real 3rd St property line 355.6 deg vs figure 355.3; real TAFB property line 355.7 vs figure 356.1; DataSF Exposition Street (Toni Stone Crossing) centerline 85.7 deg vs the figure's Exposition axis 84.9 deg, with 0.2 m offset at mid-block. (4) METHOD. Each block's fill (base colour plus hatched upper-building zone) was isolated by colour saturation inside a pixel window, its outer contour extracted and simplified (approxPolyDP, 1% of perimeter), transformed, and then any vertex within 3 m of a recorded lot line of 8719A006, 8719A003, 8719A005, 8719A007, 8719A009, 8719A010, 8719C001, 8719C002, 8719C004 or 8719D001 was snapped onto that line, so street frontages and shared edges are the Assessor's lines rather than the figure's 1-3 m of contour noise. Cross-checked against an independent trace of the same block on Figure 1.1 (p.10) through its own transform fitted the same way (RMS 1.1 m). (5) CHECKER. Registered in src/verify_block_fill.py under site 'mission_rock' (pixel window and colour rule recorded there); CI prints the IoU against the figure's own fill on every run. D1 SPECIFICS: Block D was traced as one fill (5 raw vertices reduced to its 4 dominant corners; 3 corners on lot 8719A006's 3rd Street and Mission Rock Street lines; area 93,656 sf vs 97,498 sf in the 2012 parcel table, -3.9%). The D1/D2 split is read from the same Figure 6.2 render: D1 is the L-shaped residential zone drawn in Figure 1.1 (yellow) -- a 45 ft 'building wrap, all levels' strip along the whole 3rd Street frontage (the 45.00' dimension on Appendix p.190, Block D) plus the 240 ft tower zone at the 3rd St x Mission Rock St corner, whose solid outline on Figure 6.2 sits at px x=1809.5 (east edge) and px y=1883.5 (north edge) on the 300-dpi render. D1 = D within that L; area 20,480 sf, 6 vertices. Cross-check: IoU 0.70 against the yellow D1 fill traced independently on Figure 1.1 through its own transform (the 45 ft strip is only ~13 m wide, so a 1 m transform difference costs IoU quickly).
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (see digitization_method): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. The D1/D2 line is a land-use zone boundary inside one Design Controls block, not a lot line; the Appendix marks Block D's parcel dimensions as illustrative.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so joining status.csv to it would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential Mixed Use per the D4D's Land Use Plan. Max height 240 ft -- one of the three tallest towers planned for the site (tied with Blocks A and F), NOT a 'mid-rise' as sometimes described in secondary summaries. Sits at the 3rd St / Mission Rock St corner, fronting 3rd St -- 'marks the Mission Rock MUNI Metro Station along 3rd Street' per the D4D's own narrative text (Section 6.5.2). Part of the same larger Block D parcel as D2, subdivided into a residential tower (D1) and a parking structure (D2).
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted future block -- not yet built, no distinct real parcel yet. See accuracy_caveat.
